script.title: Why Maruti Makes Less On More Sales #shorts

segments.text: Maruti grew revenue by 26%, so why are its profit margins shrinking?
For decades, Maruti was India's undisputed king of cheap, reliable hatchbacks like the Alto.
A ₹5 lakh car gave them massive volume, but wafer-thin profits per vehicle.
Today, aspirational Indians are ditching budget hatchbacks for ₹15 lakh SUVs loaded with tech.
To keep up, Maruti is battling fierce discount wars while redesigning entire lineups.
Higher manufacturing costs and mark-to-market losses ate away at their fresh revenue jump.
In India's auto market, selling bigger cars doesn't mean printing easier money.
Which leaves investors asking the exact same puzzle:
